requirement:
`habeas status` MUST group the selected requirement and example judgments marked
FIXME by issue reference and report how many distinct judgments each issue
affects. It MUST recognize `#123` and `owner/repo#123` within recorded FIXME
strings, including `FIXME(...)` and explanatory text. A GitHub issue URL such as
`https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/123` MUST identify the same issue as
`owner/repo#123`. Issue numbers MUST be positive, complete numeric tokens with
leading zeros normalized; repository spelling MUST remain case-sensitive, and
unqualified and qualified references MUST remain distinct.

A judgment MUST count at most once for each issue, even when that issue occurs
repeatedly or in several FIXME strings. A judgment naming several issues MUST
count in each corresponding group. Judgments with no recognized issue in any
FIXME string MUST be counted once in a separate "FIXME without an issue" group.
Issue groups MUST be ordered by decreasing affected-judgment count, then by
normalized reference; the group without an issue MUST follow them. A supplied
selection MUST restrict these counts to the selected subjects.

`--verbose` MUST list the full name and kind of every judgment in each issue
group and in the group without an issue, along with its original FIXME strings.
The summary MUST include valid FIXME determinations even when other evidence
checks fail; grouping MUST NOT hide their validation findings. Malformed
determinations MUST remain validation errors under {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the sources meet `requirements.cli.fixme_summary`. I found no acknowledged gaps (no FIXME markers), so the determination is `true`.

**Implementation**
- `status_markdown_with_options` (`src/commands.rs`) walks the selected non-term definitions. It filters them by glob and validates the glob. For each one it loads the evidence and calls `fixmes.add(name, kind, evidence.fixme_entries())` before any row filtering, so every FIXME judgment is counted whether or not it is listed individually.
- `LoadedDetailEvidence::load` (`src/index.rs`) parses the determination straight from the record, independently of the error list. Valid FIXME entries therefore survive stale-input or coverage failures. A malformed determination fails `Judgment::from_value` (`src/judgment.rs`), which yields no entries and leaves the row `Invalid`. Its validation findings are still printed in the "Validation findings" section.
- `FixmeSummary::add` and `render` (`src/fixme.rs`) implement the grouping.
  - Each judgment is a single record keyed by name, and `issue_references` returns a `BTreeSet`, so a judgment counts at most once per issue and once in each issue it names.
  - Judgments with no recognized issue go into `without_issue`. That group is printed after the issue groups and is counted once per judgment.
  - Groups are sorted by descending count, then by normalized reference string.
  - `--verbose` lists each judgment's full name, kind, and original FIXME strings, HTML-escaped, in every issue group and in the "FIXME without an issue" group.
- `issue_references` handles the parsing rules.
  - Its regex recognizes `#N`, `owner/repo#N`, and `https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/N`, and normalizes the URL form to `owner/repo#N`.
  - It requires complete numeric tokens: it rejects `#12abc` and `##123`, and rejects a match preceded by an alphanumeric, `_`, `/` or `#`.
  - It strips leading zeros and drops zero-only numbers such as `#000`.
  - It keeps repository spelling case-sensitive, and keeps unqualified references distinct from qualified ones.
- `main.rs` passes `--verbose` and the selection through to `status_markdown_with_options`.

**Tests**
- The `fixme_fixture` helper in `tests/commands.rs` builds four FIXME judgments (three requirements and one example) that cover:
  - leading zeros (`#00123`, `#000456`) and URL-versus-qualified equivalence;
  - case-sensitive repository names (`Rust-Lang/rust#456` versus `rust-lang/rust#456`);
  - repeated references within one judgment;
  - a judgment naming several issues;
  - non-issues (`#000`, `#12abc`, `##123`);
  - an HTML-injection string.
- `status_groups_fixme_judgments_by_distinct_normalized_issue` checks:
  - counts and ordering, including a tie on count broken by reference;
  - the "without an issue" group coming last;
  - that unnormalized forms do not appear;
  - that individual subjects are hidden in default mode;
  - that `--all` shows FIXME rows and the same summary.
- `verbose_status_lists_fixme_judgments_and_globs_scope_issue_groups` checks:
  - that verbose output lists names, kinds, and the original strings;
  - that HTML is escaped;
  - that a selection restricts the counts, both to one issue and to the no-issue group.
- `tests/outcomes.rs` covers three more cases.
  - `malformed_fixme_is_invalid_and_reports_the_required_shape` checks that a malformed FIXME is `Invalid`, shows its error, and produces no `affects` summary.
  - `fixme_does_not_hide_stale_inputs_or_uncovered_references` checks that a stale input leaves the row `Invalid`, while the summary still shows `#125` and the finding is not hidden.
  - `valid_fixme_remains_visible_in_status_info_and_book` checks that a valid FIXME still appears in the summary.

**Minor observations (not gaps)**
- Ties are ordered by string comparison of the normalized reference, so `#123` sorts before `#45`. The spec's "normalized reference" ordering is ambiguous on this, and the test pins the string ordering.
- The accessors `fixme_entries` in `src/index.rs` and `src/judgment.rs`, and the part of `load` that keeps FIXME entries despite errors, are marked with `cli.status`, `index.state` and `ci.outcomes` rather than `fixme_summary`. They are thin plumbing, and `cli.status` itself defers to this requirement, so I did not treat this as a marking gap.

The `habeas` CLI MUST use `clap` to define and parse its commands and options.

The `mdbook` subcommand MUST act as the mdBook preprocessor for HTML books, rendering requirement definitions and linked reference badges. This project's `book.toml` MUST configure `cargo habeas mdbook` as the `habeas` preprocessor, using a repository-local Cargo alias for `cargo run --release -p habeas --`. Consumer books MUST continue to invoke the installed `habeas mdbook` CLI directly.

Running `habeas setup` in an existing Cargo and mdBook project MUST add Habeas as a dev dependency, configure `habeas mdbook` as its preprocessor, add the badge stylesheet, and create `tests/habeas.rs` that calls `habeas::validate()`. Repeating setup MUST avoid duplicate configuration and MUST NOT overwrite a differing test or stylesheet. Setup MUST NOT install or modify agent skills.

`habeas status [<selection>] [--all] [--verbose]` MUST consider requirements and named examples matched by the {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`; without a selection it MUST consider every definition. By default, it MUST list matching definitions in full-name order when their evidence is missing, has a false determination, or fails the same evidence and reference checks as `habeas::validate()`. It MUST summarize FIXME judgments under {cite}`requirements.cli.fixme_summary`, with accepted FIXME subjects listed individually only when `--verbose` or `--all` is selected. `--all` MUST list every matching definition with its kind and evidence state. Every form MUST show validation findings, including repository-wide Rust function coverage findings, work from within a Cargo and mdBook project, and report invalid arguments or a supplied selection matching no definition clearly.

When `habeas status` or `habeas status --all` displays a Markdown table, it MUST left-align and space-pad the Definition and Evidence columns so every row, including the header and separator row, has its `|` column delimiters in the same positions. Column widths MUST be determined by the widest displayed cell in each column.

`habeas status` and the mdBook requirements index MUST generate their Definition/Evidence Markdown tables through the same renderer. That renderer MUST calculate column widths, align the columns, and display the same evidence-state labels in both outputs. Callers MAY select different definitions and supply different kind-labeled name cells so mdBook can link to detail pages.

`habeas info <selection>` MUST show the requirements and named examples matched by the {term}`requirements.references.definition_selection`. It MUST print matches in full-name order as Markdown with the same kind-labeled definition, Validation findings, Rationale, and Inputs structure and evidence states as mdBook detail pages, including readable output for missing or invalid evidence. It MUST work without a requirements index directive and report an invalid selection or no matches clearly. Habeas's bundled agent guidance MUST tell agents they can use this command to inspect a requirement or named example.

`habeas add-input` MUST accept exactly one evidence target: `--for-requirement <full-name>` or `--for-example <full-name>`. It MUST accept exactly one input mode: `--file-range`, `--rust-item`, or `--requirements`. It MUST use the same input schema and resolution rules as validation. Repeating a selector for a target MUST refresh its existing input rather than add a duplicate; an unchanged input MUST leave the record unchanged. The command MUST report every input it adds or refreshes. It MUST create a missing target record with a pending determination. Whenever it changes a record, it MUST leave `determination` false with a nonempty rationale indicating that review is pending.
`habeas add-input --file-range <file>:<start>-<end>` MUST add or refresh one file-range input containing the current raw lines in the inclusive range. It MUST reject a missing file or invalid range.

`habeas add-input --rust-item <rust-file>:<line>` MUST parse the file with `syn` and add or refresh one Rust-item input for every explicit item declared on that line. An item with a declared name is declared on the line containing that name; an item without one is declared on the line containing its distinctive keyword or introducer, such as `use` or `impl`. Each input MUST store the selected `rust_file` under the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the item's syntactic `rust_item` selector, and its complete raw source lines. The command MUST report every selected item and reject a line on which no item is declared.

`habeas add-input --requirements <selection>` MUST add or refresh one requirements input containing the matched full names and their concatenated raw declaration sources. It MUST report the matched names in expansion order and reject a selection that matches no requirement or named example.

Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.

The bundled requirements skill MUST direct agents adding or changing user-visible behavior in a Habeas project to draft stable requirement IDs and exact text, obtain the user's agreement, and install the agreed requirements in the mdBook before writing implementation or test code. It MUST direct agents to review substantive changes to agreed obligations with the user. The bootstrap skill MUST require user review of requirements inferred from existing code before installing them. The evidence skill MUST accept missing evidence or truthful false judgments from the harness while implementation is pending; it MUST NOT direct the supervising agent to write placeholder evidence itself.
